newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cabinet wants urgent action in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cabinet wants urgent action in Karachi.

text.p: The Pakistani cabinet told the Interior Ministry on Friday to take emergency measures to fight renewed violence in the industrial port city of Karachi, a government statement said.

It said a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif "noted with concern recent incidents of terrorism in Karachi", which has seen a surge of violence in recent weeks amid renewed tension between the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its breakaway Haqiqi faction.

The cabinet directed the Interior Ministry "to take emergency measures in co-ordination with the concerned law-enforcement and security agencies and in consultation with the provincial government", the statement said.

It quoted Sharif as telling the cabinet that law and order in Karachi, Pakistan's commercial centre and capital of the southern province of Sindh, was "a matter of high priority" for his four-month-old government.

"The members of the cabinet were unanimously of the view that elements unhappy with new signs of stability and progress in Pakistan were engineering situations to create despondency and a sense of insecurity in Karachi," it said.
It said Sharif expressed "the strongest resolve of the government" to ensure peace and security in Karachi.
More than 100 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian unrest in Karachi so far this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.

The MQM, long involved in a struggle with the security forces as well as with the Haqiqi faction, was brought into a coalition government led by Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League Party after national and provincial elections in February.
